question: Can a lightweight two-step fine-tuning of an LLM (to use retrieved text) and of a retriever (to return what the LLM prefers) beat off-the-shelf retrieval-augmented LMs on knowledge-intensive tasks?
hypothesis: Combining off-the-shelf LLMs and retrievers is sub-optimal; fine-tuning each half separately against the other will help, and doing both will help most.
contributions: RA-DIT: retrieval-augmented instruction tuning of the LM (RA-IT) plus LM-supervised fine-tuning of the retriever's query encoder, as two separate steps
Generalises LSR to multi-task instruction data mixed with unsupervised text completion
State-of-the-art 0-shot and few-shot results on knowledge-intensive benchmarks with LLaMA 65B, competitive with Atlas 11B in 64-shot fine-tuning
Ablations of LM fine-tuning, retriever fine-tuning, model size, retriever choice, parallel vs concatenated chunks, and retrieval corpus

method.summary: LLaMA (7B/13B/65B) is instruction-tuned on 20 datasets with a retrieved 'Background:' chunk prepended (top-3 chunks, one fine-tuning instance per chunk). Separately, the DRAGON+ query encoder is fine-tuned with a KL loss against LM-derived LSR scores over top-10 chunks, using 95% unsupervised corpus data and 5% multi-task instruction data. At inference the top-10 chunks are each prepended and the LM outputs are mixed by retriever score (REPLUG-style parallel augmentation).
method.task: retrieval-augmented instruction tuning for knowledge-intensive tasks (open-domain QA, KILT tasks, MMLU)

models.name: DRAGON+
models.architecture: dual-encoder dense retriever, dot-product similarity; only the query encoder is fine-tuned

training.objective: LM: next-token loss on output segment only, L(D_L) = -sum_i sum_j log p_LM(y_i | c_ij o x_i). Retriever: KL(p_R(c|x) || p_LSR(c|x,y)) with p_LSR proportional to exp(p_LM(y|c o x)/tau)
training.lr_schedule: LM: cosine. 64-shot task fine-tuning: linear from 1e-5 to 1e-6
training.batch_size: LM: 64 (7B), 128 (13B), 128 (65B). Retriever: 32 per GPU. 64-shot: 32 for RA-DIT 13B and 65B
training.steps: LM: 500 scheduled steps; best checkpoint at 500 (7B), 400 (13B), 300 (65B) by early stopping. 64-shot: 100 steps, best at 50
training.epochs: Retriever: 1 epoch over 95% corpus + 5% MTI data
training.regularisation: early stopping on average dev score of the 6 KILT dev tasks, evaluated every 100 steps (every 50 for 64-shot)
training.hardware: LM: 8, 16, 64 A100 GPUs for 7B, 13B, 65B. Retriever: 16 A100 GPUs

other.k_tilde: top-3 chunks used to build LM fine-tuning instances
other.retriever_top_k: top-10 chunks and LSR scores computed once with LLaMA 65B + DRAGON+ and not updated during R-ft
other.retriever_validation: MRR every 500 steps on a combined validation set of the 10-task MTI data
other.retriever_mixture: 95% corpus data + 5% MTI data (5% or 10% MTI worked best in early tests)

inference.decoding: multi-choice: weighted mean probability per choice over chunks, take the highest. Generation: decode with each augmented prompt independently, sum weighted probability per unique answer, output the highest
inference.samples: single run; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: 'Background: {retrieved passage}\n\n' prepended to the task template (Tables 10, 12); 0-shot and 5-shot in-context, 64-shot fine-tuned
inference.retrieval: top-10 chunks (k=10) from the 399M corpus, each prepended separately, outputs mixed by renormalised retriever score; queries from manual templates (Table 12); no retrieval for commonsense tasks

parameters.scoring_functions: nll, nll char, nll token, nll compl (per task, Table 11)

limits: Hyperparameters and checkpoints are selected on the dev sets of 6 KILT tasks, so few-shot results on those tasks assume in-domain dev data; only 4 of 10 eval tasks are genuinely few-shot (Section 3.3).
Retriever fine-tuning gains are small (0.6 points on dev average at 5-shot); the authors do not report variance or seeds.
Retrieval queries come from manually written templates; automatic task-specific query generation is left to future work (footnote 5).
Iterating dual tuning for one or two rounds gave no further gains; multi-step RA-DIT left to future work.
RA-DIT 65B is compared with Atlas 11B; sizes are not matched, and the 64-shot protocols differ (one multi-task model vs per-task models).
Parallel augmentation is computationally costly for few-shot prompts; fine-tuning with chunk concatenation is not explored.
LLaMA-1 era models; requires LM token probabilities to compute LSR scores and to ensemble chunks.
The authors report lower 0-shot LLaMA 65B NQ/TQA than Touvron et al. because they use exact match instead of answer-string containment.
